gloss: ritual burning of old charms and talismans

definitions.gloss: ritual burning of old charms, talismans, and sacred objects
definitions.explanation: A Shinto or Buddhist rite in which old お{札|ふだ}, お{守|まも}り, and other sacred objects are respectfully burned at a shrine or temple, returning them to the gods. It is held so that items containing spiritual power are not simply thrown away.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}いお{札|ふだ}をお{焚|た}き{上|あ}げに{出|だ}す。
examples.english: I take my old talismans to be ritually burned.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}でお{焚|た}き{上|あ}げが{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: A ritual burning was held at the shrine.

examples.japanese: {正月|しょうがつ}が{過|す}ぎると、{古|ふる}いお{守|まも}りをお{焚|た}き{上|あ}げしてもらう。
examples.english: After New Year's passes, I have my old amulets ritually burned.

notes:
From the verb {焚|た}く (to burn, to kindle) with the honorific お prefix. Frequently used with する: お{焚|た}き{上|あ}げする, お{焚|た}き{上|あ}げしてもらう.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- Most common in early January, when New Year's decorations and the previous year's お{守|まも}り are burned
- The well-known fire festival どんど{焼|や}き is one form of お{焚|た}き{上|あ}げ
- Reflects the belief that sacred objects should be returned to the divine, not discarded as ordinary trash
